Params: "As you've seen in the video just now, the Atlantic Eye, one of the largest scientific research and infrastructure complexes in human history, is being raised to its highest defense posture."
"The World Government has decided to establish new defense military districts within the Transatlantic Economic Community's jurisdiction."
Every seat beneath the dome is taken. The instructor at the podium speaks in a measured voice, but each word lands like a heavy blow.
"And one year from today, F.O.S. will be hosting the Military Combat Competition."
"The winner will earn a direct promotion to the military districts within the Transatlantic Economic Community. No sponsorship is required."
The moment the last word leaves the podium, the hall bursts into a wave of murmurs and exclamations.
No sponsorship is required... A direct F.O.S. route to promotion?!

The Transatlantic Economic Community... I hear it's got tons of zero-point energy projects, cutting-edge facilities, Atlantis... and the Atlantic Eye. Quick promotions and a stellar resume... It's the posting everyone's scrambling to get into.
But weren't these normally reserved for TEC people? I thought the families there had their own referral systems.
Sounds like those days are over. In an academy founded by Mr. Dominik, opportunities should go to those who prove themselves.
Excitement passes through the seats like a swelling tide. Only one young man sinks deeper into his shoulders, as though trying to squeeze himself dry and disappear from the flood.
Military Combat Competition... Why does it have to be a Military Combat Competition...
Live fire, right? It's probably live fire. Getting tagged in a sim won't kill you, but man, it's going to sting.
The words slip out in a low murmur as he glances toward the cadet sitting beside him, hoping for a shred of comfort to hold onto.
Hey, this is optional, isn't it? No one's forcing us to sign up... right?
Hey, why aren't you saying anything?
No, no, I'm just... I'm a little freaked out, and there's no one else to talk to...
Actually, now that you mention it... I know just about everyone in Tactics by sight. I heard there were some special transfers recently, with entry scores that are crazy high...
Don't tell me you're one of them?
He recoils as if doused in cold water, shrinking back into his seat to nurse his worries alone.
So he does not notice the girl's figure, half-hidden in the shadows, leaning forward... and that fierce, restrained hunger in her eyes.
Her arms are crossed, her gaze locked on the words on stage. She does not move.
A chance that doesn't need anyone's approval.

"Some of you may not be fully familiar with the Transatlantic Economic Community's infrastructure. Today, we're pleased to have a councilor from the Transatlantic Economic Community here to answer any questions you may have."
The strain in her voice makes him startle. He darts a look at the girl beside him, then returns his gaze to the stage.
A man in a sharp suit walks to the podium, his smile as flawlessly tailored as his attire. Behind him, the display shifts to a sheet of deep blue.
Now then, on behalf of the Transatlantic Economic Community, allow me to extend an invitation to all of you, the future's brightest minds.

In the TEC, you'll see tower clusters rising like coral reefs, maglev rails weaving between them, vehicles glowing with bio-luminescence. And in the years ahead, we'll be building Constellia, a city dedicated to art, preserving the very best of humanity's Golden Age.
And there's the Atlantic Eye. She has tamed this planet's most savage currents and will become the eye through which Earth looks up to the stars.
After covering the scenic beauty of the Transatlantic Economic Community, the councilor moves to the next topic.

I'm sure you're all familiar with the Enlightenment Scholarship program, a grant established jointly by the Transatlantic Economic Community and several research groups. Its associated frontier research fund has been running for years now.
Over the past few years, the Transatlantic Economic Community's partnerships with these research groups have progressed well, with several results already proving themselves in the market.
To ensure these benefits reach the wider world, and to keep supporting the best research talent out there, I've been asked by the Community to make this announcement:
Starting this semester, scholarship funding will be doubled, and research grants will be made available to all labs working on Transatlantic Economic Community development projects.
Sure, but they actually follow through. I came from a place with almost no funding. It was this scholarship that got me into F.O.S. Without it, you'd probably have a different neighbor right now.
You remember when your advisor's project ran out of money?
I heard their foundation covered the gap, no conditions attached.
All you have to do is focus on being exceptional. Equipment, labs, whatever you need, leave it to us.
And beyond the competition, you're always welcome to visit the Transatlantic Economic Community.
The auditorium breaks into thunderous applause. The young man lifts his hands to join in, but they freeze in the air. One look at the girl beside him is enough to silence him completely.
The ship's prow that had pressed into the wind is drawn back. She settles into her seat, upright and still, like a blade sheathed.
Hey, you okay? Not feeling well?
Just as he decides to keep quiet and mind his own business, the cold voice rings out on its own.
F.O.S. is Professor Dominik's academy, for the whole world. It's not owned by anyone.
I just don't want to see their hands reaching in here too.
Ana, calm down. This isn't the right place.
Wait, hang on. I want to check the requirements for the scholarship and research fund.
Why would you take handouts from people like that?
You spend their money for all it's worth. That's the whole idea. No reason to feel bad about it.
The girl rises and slips out without another word, leaving an awkward space between the young man and her companion.
He opens his mouth, then thinks better of it and stays silent. He has a faint feeling that her words and the weight on his own mind don't come from the same kind of fear.
At the back of the hall, a white-haired figure clutching a stack of files is already turning to leave.
The Transatlantic Economic Community... of all places?

On the screen, the promotional video shows a sweeping view of the underwater city. The metropolis glows beneath the sea's shimmering light, transit rails threading through its expanse, cutting-edge bionic machines working alongside human hands in the deep.
—That is the place where she grew up.
Excuse me, are you here for the event? I'll need to check your—
—That is also the place she is not ready to go back to.
She puts the churning feelings aside and keeps walking.
The broadcast screen is switched off with a casual gesture. The young visiting instructor is still at his desk after hours, organizing the student grade records passed on by a senior instructor.
Tomorrow's your first class, young man. Hope it goes well.
His finger pauses over a peculiar entry. It's a standard three-person assault mission, completed solo by a single student.
The teamwork score should be zero, but this says...
He remembers the pointed remark the senior instructor made during the handover.
"She's a Helio. I'm close to retirement, so I'm not about to make waves with the TEC."
...Heh. One of the four families? Of course.
He is still frowning at the screen when an incoming call lights up his terminal. One look at the name, and he encrypts the channel without a word.
Still running anti-eavesdropping protocols. Glad to see that.
So, trade the General Staff circus for a quiet corner at F.O.S... How's that working out?
...You keep up that tone and I'm hanging up on you, Hassen.
You really need to work on that temper. Don't give them more reason to call you "too impulsive, not cut out for real work."
Using Ballard's words against me. Nice.
I'd take "not cut out for real work" over being in the same building as Collins any day.
Those two aren't on the same side, I can promise you that.
You know how the first one is. The second one... that fight you had at the promotion debate? Still remember it?

"Humanity is on the verge of unification, and traditional military strategy is outdated. The future doesn't need courage or intelligence; it needs people who understand human nature and know how to play the game."
Never heard someone make spinelessness sound so pretty.
Pretty words have a way of getting people what they're after.
The World Government needs money, and Collins' backers have it. That deal was done before the debate even started.
He puts the student records down on the desk with a thud.
...I'm just done putting up with it.
Come on, everyone knows you've got talent and a temper, the brass included. The General Staff never ruled one way or the other. That's them going easy on you, isn't it?
And yet I'm still here at F.O.S.
It's one batch of students. You'll be back when it's over, whether you want to or not.
Besides, F.O.S. is a decent place to keep your head down. It's Professor Dominik's academy. Even the people who'd love to stick their fingers in think twice before trying.
Let me correct you there. Inside these walls, we can be fair. But outside... it's still their game, even for Dominik's academy.
A TEC councilor came to F.O.S. today and announced a bunch of new funding initiatives.
Nothing with them is free. You know how they operate.
Silence settles over both ends of the line. After a moment, the easy warmth in the voice on the other side fades into something lower and heavier.
If it comes to that, the Parliament won't just sit back.
As a colleague, let me know if anything comes up.
As a friend, I'd tell you to stay out of trouble, but we both know you won't. So at least watch your back.
Good luck with the teaching, Instructor Wells.
The call ends. Wells exhales slowly and uncrosses his legs. Hassen is one of the few people allowed to see his guard drop, even slightly.
He adjusts his posture and returns his attention to the record on his desk. Almost at that same instant, a knock sounds at the door.
A white-haired girl enters, comes to attention with a sharp salute, and wastes no time on pleasantries.
Adelyde Helio, second year Tactics. I need a grade fixed, instructor.
Mission 7, squad exercise. I went solo, with no partner. But my teamwork score says 100.
I'd like you to change it back to zero, sir.
Wells studies the student before him. That Helio, the one he had mentally dismissed as another family connection not long ago.
Yet now she has come to him, asking him to erase the perfect score on her record.
100's a pretty nice number. Your other grades are excellent. With this, you'd have a spotless record.
But zero on teamwork? That'll drag everything down.
Wells tosses the hook and waits.
I don't need anything that's not mine.
Her reply is clear, immediate, without a flicker of doubt. Wells does not pause either.
I respect your choice. And I respect what F.O.S. stands for.
Alright. Back to zero it is.
He revises the record in full view of her, then closes the file.
Before you go, let me introduce myself. Wells. Starting tomorrow, I'll be your tactical training instructor.
Fair warning: teamwork is non-negotiable in my class. You keep that zero, you don't graduate. End of story.
My solo performance is above the squad average—
Taking on a team mission by yourself... That's not impressive, that's reckless. And reckless gets people killed.
Understood. I won't neglect the teamwork score, but I expect F.O.S. to apply its rules consistently. I won't accept another mismatch between what I do and what gets put on paper.
The instructor's easy answer catches Adelyde off guard.
Wells lets his gaze drop to the roster, where her full name is printed clearly: Adelyde Helio.
First thing tomorrow, I'm reassigning every student who doesn't have a partner. That includes you.
Wells lifts his eyes and meets the student's gaze.
No problems with that, Miss Helio?
Wells turns back to the file, pauses on the entry he just zeroed out, then continues to the next page.
Another student's profile draws his attention. This one came from a disadvantaged region in the South Atlantic, took the hardest general admissions track, and scored among the top in the world.
The file photo shows a girl in uniform, a bright smile on her face.
At the back of the dossier sits a page titled External Background Review, written in clean, official language.

[Due to unresolved background associations on this student's record, the following is recommended: restrict this student's access to command track courses; competition registration requires a faculty guarantor.]
There is no signature, only a filing code.
Wells pulls the sheet from the file, folds it once, and tosses it toward the machine at his side.
The shredder takes it with a quiet hum.
The Next Morning\nOutdoor Shooting Range, F.O.S.

It is a major training day for the second-years, with paired cross-cover drills on the schedule. The warm-up area hums with activity, cadets moving in pairs through stretches and exercises, calling out reps to each other.
A white-haired figure walks straight through the crowd, heading for the equipment rack at the edge of the range.
Look, that's the Helio heir... I heard she took on squad missions all by herself.

That's just the start. When the Atlantic Eye leak went down, her family wasted no time throwing the Copperfields under the bus. Heartless bunch. Wouldn't surprise me if she put a knife in your back one day too.
Shh, keep your voice down. If she's really that untouchable, the smart play is to be friendly. Maybe someday she'll be running the family...
The murmurs drift her way, just loud enough to catch, but Adelyde ignores them.
She props a leg on the rack and works through her stretches alone, the ones meant to be done with a partner.
Reaching down, folding forward, the kind of move that needs a light hand at your back.
This is her twelfth major training day at F.O.S., and she has long since learned to warm up solo, improvising with equipment and angles to replace the missing partner.
Two years ago, it was Rusalka who helped her through these same motions.
It was another warm spring. In the manor's back garden, leaves unfurled and flowers pushed through the soil once more.
Life and death always seemed to walk side by side. The one who had planted them closed her eyes for the last time on a spring day, just as the flowers came into bloom.
The family held a brief, dignified funeral. When it was over, the guests dispersed, all except Adelyde, who remained before her mother's grave.
She opened the notebook she had kept for almost ten years, turned to the last page, and wrote one final entry.
<color=#2e2825><size=35>April 2nd. Clear skies.\nMom got to see the flowers bloom.</size></color>
[April 2nd. Clear skies. Mom got to see the flowers bloom.]
Two weeks later, as Adelyde was packing her belongings, Rusalka appeared in the doorway behind her.
I don't really know... Thank you for asking, Miss Rusalka.
Adelyde pulled the last zipper closed and turned to face Rusalka.
...You came to talk me out of it, didn't you? I've already sent in my application to F.O.S.
I know losing Florence has hit you hard, but I still hope you'll stay.
Anything F.O.S. can teach you, the family can teach you just as well.
When I was little, my mom told me that just growing up well was enough to make her happy.
The family's always taught me to win. But if winning is the only way I know how to grow, can that really get me where I need to go?
I can't find that answer here, so I'm going to find a place where I can.
Adelyde drew a deep breath and forced the heaviness in her chest down.
I still find it hard to understand why the family did what they did during the Purge.
You're only looking at the surface. People who achieve great things learn to live with sacrifices. You'll learn too.
...I don't want to learn it right now.
Rusalka held her gaze for a long moment. There was something churning in her eyes that Adelyde could not quite decipher.
You've always been stubborn. Pushing you has never worked. I can be patient.
But even as the top candidate for succession, the family won't wait around forever.
Then wait until I graduate from F.O.S.
I'll come back with a new perspective, and look for a way to change things.
...Heh. You're free to think that way.
Nothing teaches like real experience. If you want to find out for yourself, by all means.
In the corner, she braces herself alone.
The registration desk has a long line, cadets standing in pairs, calling out their partner's name as they sign in.
A familiar voice makes her stand up straight, and she finds a dark-haired girl before her, her smile as gentle as ever, though touched by a faint, almost invisible weariness.
It's been a while... How have you been?
They trade a few polite lines, and then the conversation stalls. Neither of them speaks. They never used to need to search for words... not when that other girl was still between them.
...Cross-cover is a two-person drill. Pair up with me, Ade.
Nothing's changed. If the Helio and Spelmin heirs pair up at F.O.S., both sides will get wind of it.
Could be good, could be trouble. I can't bet on it right now. Neither side is playing their cards.
Helentine nods, a bitter edge to the gesture. Neither of them needs to say more.
Your sister's at F.O.S. too. I'm not going to drag you both down with me.
..."Drag." When did it become like this between us?
Another long silence falls. It has become familiar territory, settling between them as it always does.
Every training day, Helentine finds Adelyde. And every time, the same pattern repeats. A few words, then a break, and the quiet takes over.
They're only three meters apart, but the space between them feels like a wound that will not close.
I heard you've been doing three people's worth of mission work all by yourself. Training twelve hours a day, almost every day.
You have to take good care of yourself.
Sis! Over here, registration's about to close!
A girl's voice calls from the far end of the line. A flash of platinum hair gleams in the sun, bright with an almost unreasonable vitality.
Once in her life, that same light had crashed into Adelyde's world with equal force.
Helentine gives Adelyde one final glance, then turns and melts into the crowd.
The queue sorts itself into pairs. Adelyde remains alone, working through her next round of stretches with mechanical precision.
Ten minutes later, she moves to the prep area. Distant gunfire echoes across the range. She leans against the barrier and loads magazines by herself.
An unremarkable cadet settles into a crouch next to her, hands moving to load a magazine. Her eyes are fixed on the firing lane ahead.

Her gear is standard issue, secured neatly at the hip, every button fastened in place. Her height, face, and clothing are all utterly average, so average that it almost reads as intentional. She's the kind of person who disappears the moment she steps into a crowd.
So, where did we leave off?
About a year ago, the family sent out "amnesty" emails to those swept up in the Purge. Probably an attempt to bring capable people back to the Atlantic Eye.
I pulled a few from the family's internal data. They had recipient addresses attached.
Right. You passed them to me, and I took it from there.
I traced it through my family's network and found out the exiles ended up in the South Atlantic.
That's the maritime intelligence background for you.
Don't discount the legwork I put in.
Anyway, the person you're looking for is likely among them. Specifically, among those who worked at your family's branch facilities.
Energy engineering, if I remember correctly. Same as the rest.
Couldn't tell you exactly what they are doing there. Pushing further would've crossed a line.
The only thing I found was a strike report from about a year ago. It lines up with those amnesty emails you mentioned.
So the "amnesty" was dressed up as goodwill, but really it was some kind of trap...?
Except some people did make it back to the TEC through it. It's just that...
"Arakna" isn't on that list, is she? She never made it back, and after that, her trail stops cold.
Another volley cracks across the range. Greta lowers her voice.
Sometimes not knowing the whole truth is better for your own good.
If that's really what happened, then it was settled two years ago. Neither of us can change it now.
Of course. You've already gotten me more than enough. I appreciate it.
Your payment will be sent as usual. Don't worry.
You know that's not what I mean.
Two years, chasing a dead lead, and you've ended up alone. Is it really worth it?
Moving forward doesn't mean closing your eyes.
Another one of your sayings I can't make sense of.
At least I've still got someone to talk to, and that's you.
We're not friends. We have a deal. I just want to study, graduate, and earn some side money while I'm at it.
Adelyde gives a small shrug, dropping the matter. A short word of parting, and then Greta steps into the stream of shifting cadets, vanishing from sight almost instantly.
Adelyde adjusts her gear, picks up her gun, and walks away.
The bell has barely finished ringing when the young instructor pushes through the door, right on time, and drops the roster onto the desk.
Afternoon, everyone. I'm Wells. I'll be teaching your tactical training course from now on.
Quick administrative note: there's a new student joining us this semester, transferred in through the special admissions exam. She'll be in this class with you.
Anyone without a partner will be assigned one by me.
A ripple of low murmurs runs through the room. Everyone knows who is always left without a partner.
Short, blue hair dances in the wind. For a moment, Adelyde thinks her eyes are playing tricks on her.
Arakna Sorano, from the Transatlantic Economic Community. Looking forward to studying with all of you.
Her heart clenches. She had pictured a hundred ways they might meet again, but none of them took place here.
Arakna Sorano will be assigned to Adelyde Helio's team. Any objections?
Her own voice sounds tight to her ears. The blue-haired girl by the teacher's desk turns her head at the sound.
Two years have passed. Adelyde searches those eyes for any trace of the docks, the airship, the Wishing Platform, the Interstellar Drift Bottle... only to find nothing.
The eyes that once held an entire galaxy now regard her with a quiet emptiness, as though she were a complete stranger.
